The normal Arterial Blood Gas and D-Dimer levels effectively rule out pulmonary embolism and severe respiratory acidosis, while the normal Liver Ultrasound suggests your abdominal girth and shortness of breath are likely due to ascites caused by the ovarian mass rather than liver failure. Since we have confirmed a large ovarian mass with secondary ascites but have not yet determined its malignant potential, do you have any history of irregular vaginal bleeding, pelvic pain, or known family history of ovarian or breast cancer?
